int16_int32.mma: none: A100/H100 tensor cores have no INT16 MMA
int16_int32.note: a single 16 x 16-bit product exceeds 2^31; 12-bit limbs give N <= 128, 11-bit N <= 512

int12_int32.note: N <= 128 defeats deferred reduction; no instruction to run it on

bf16_fp32.note: BF16 holds 8 significant bits so limbs are still 8-bit; exact sums only below 2^24 -> N < 256 at half the INT8 rate

fp16_fp32.note: 11-bit limbs, N < 4 before the FP32 significand is exhausted

fp8_fp32.note: 4-bit limbs quadruple the limb count (16x the MACs of 8-bit) for a 2x rate: never pays

rs_matrix_ntt.basis: Reed-Solomon n=16384/k=4096 (the protocols' Ligero code) as two-stage dense matrix DFTs on tensor cores (TensorFHE-style O(N sqrt N)): interpolate k = 64 x 64 (2 x 64 MACs per payload symbol), evaluate n = 128 x 128 (2 x 128 per codeword symbol); twiddle multiplies (k + n per row) on SIMT

brakedown_expander.basis: Brakedown/Spielman expander code, 20 base MACs per codeword symbol (explore.pcs assumption), SpMM gather (TensorZKP 5.2); changes the Ligero test to Brakedown's (rate 0.65, distance 0.07: more opened columns, explore.pcs.brakedown_row) -- not the protocols' code

rs_ntt_simt.basis: the SIMT-priced baseline: butterflies as F_t mults on SIMT (accounting._ntt_ops)

flips.Goldilocks stays (fields lane): FLIPS on the sumcheck side and the encoding side: the 2^-128 challenge fields are 24 limbs for both families (Goldilocks^3 = 192 bits, BabyBear^6 / M31^6 = 186 bits), so challenge x challenge costs 576 MACs either way; trace x challenge is 96 vs 192 and encoding 16 vs 64 MACs per base product, committed bytes halve. The SIMT penalty (EXT_MULT_COST 17 x 0.5 vs 6) that kept Goldilocks does not exist on tensor cores. Caveats: +9% lookups / +4% committed columns (F1/F3/F4 repairs, unverified by z3), degree-6 extensions unshipped in Plonky3/stwo, M31 needs a circle FFT.
flips.Ligero stays (pcs lane): holds, with the encoder changed: the RS code is kept but encoded as a two-stage dense matrix DFT on tensor cores (O(N sqrt N) MACs, 287 base MACs per symbol); the SIMT NTT was the largest field_ops line and is now a small fraction of the sumcheck work. Brakedown's expander code is 14x fewer MACs but gather-bound (9% of peak, TensorZKP encoder).
flips.VOLE out (hash-based only): the ruling changed (designated verifier in scope pending LPN); on tensor cores the online prover is SIMT-bound (Hadamards) and the batch check is a tiny matmul; the dense dual-LPN matmul is not viable, the d=10 primal code is a gather. Communication (667 kB/VU) stays the binding constraint.
flips.hashing is the bottleneck (SIMT lanes: c: flips for A when the hash runs at >= 50 GB/s: the hash bucket is below the matmul bucket at 17% utilisation; for B (6.7 GB hashed per batch) it stays the largest bucket below 100 GB/s.

assumptions: Every figure is an ESTIMATE from the module docstring's cost model over the WP2 checker census and the fields lane's small-field deltas; the only measurements are TensorZKP's (H100) and the candidates' recorded CPU runs, used for calibration only.

A limb product is UINT8 x UINT8 -> INT32; an element of b bits is ceil(b/8) limbs; products are schoolbook convolutions (a matmul cannot Karatsuba); deferred reduction is one (dL)^2-word SIMT combine per inner product and is not converted to time (TensorZKP: < 2%).

Sumcheck: N dl^2 (terms 2^m + 8 tables) matmul MACs and N terms (2^m - 4) SIMT Hadamards over all rounds (TensorZKP Algorithm 1 and the degree-3 recipe of 5.1); the GKR tables are units x carried width per layer (accounting's CHECKER_LAYER_WIDTHS_A, an upper bound that carries every lower-depth value); the first round's F_t operands are credited.

Encoding default: RS n=16384/k=4096 as two-stage dense matrix DFTs (287 base MACs per codeword symbol on tensor cores, k + n twiddle multiplies per row on SIMT); the Ligero soundness parameters are unchanged.  Brakedown rows use explore.pcs's 20 MACs per symbol.

Time = matmul MACs / (INT8 dense peak MAC/s x utilisation) + SIMT field mults / 1e11 per s (A100; H100 x 67/19.5; 31-bit x 0.5) + hash bytes / rate + hint generation (2e4 int ops per unit at 25% of the FP32 peak).  Buckets are summed, no overlap.

Utilisation 0.17 is TensorZKP's degree-2 sumcheck fraction of the H100 INT8 peak (their kernel is HBM-bound at ~80% of 3.35 TB/s with 32-limb elements); 1.0 is the datasheet peak.  Our elements are 8-24 limbs, so the HBM floor per element is lower.
Hint generation on GPU is unmeasured; the CPU anchor (4.7 s per 4,096 units, one thread) is reported beside the estimate.

VOLE: QuickSilver online costs per multiplication check (1 ext x ext + 2 base x ext Hadamards on SIMT; two length-checks inner products on tensor cores); LPN as Wolverine's primal d=10 local code (10 F_p MACs per correlation, gather) with the dense dual matmul (k = 589,760 MACs per correlation) shown for contrast; GGM PRG at 2 x 16 B per correlation.
